compact_summary: Withheld legal floor-price product sales for one turn when deterministic town consumption proved a rebound above 1, then sold into the rebound. Gate 2 converted 56 ties to wins with zero protected regressions; Gate 3 converted 72 ties to wins but introduced one protected W->L due later market re-saturation externalities.
key_lesson: Town-consumption and floor-price ordering is a real exploitable mechanic. Immediate gain can be predicted exactly, but later shared-market saturation can reverse the competitive effect; a safe version needs a commitment condition that predicts downstream externality, not just next-turn price.
